hero.lede: A local-first agent built on the full DeepSeek Harness and extended through native plugins. The desktop build is packaged with Rust + Tauri 2 into an all-platform app (Windows/macOS/Linux); the Harness itself is not rewritten — everything is a plugin.

status.p: master already integrates the full DSH plus the native ymzz plugin: exact branding, four native themes, nine fixed-source command skills. The tagging panel and knowledge ledger are in the source and unit-tested; Windows GUI acceptance, installers and real-model inference are still unverified.
status.1p: This is the currently truthful entry. You need Node, Git, and pnpm. Steps are on the start page.
status.2p: An x64 installer is planned after the release gate. It has not been published or accepted yet.

get.pending: No public stable product installer is available. Only after you opt in and click the manual release check will this page query public GitHub release metadata.
product.p: The agent body is the hub; native skills and plugins are replaceable spokes. Added code is MIT, with no added telemetry and explicit network consent. Actual native third-party licenses and installer behavior remain release gates; this is not an official DeepSeek product.
product.1p: Built on the full DeepSeek Harness with the native layout and component positions preserved; the desktop build packages it with Rust + Tauri 2 into an all-platform app that owns only window, install, update and lifecycle. The Harness itself is not rewritten.
product.2p: One native ymzz plugin registers brand/theme slots,9 pinned instruction skills and real DSH approval-gated tasks. Reviewed updates currently mean signed local staging only, not a live install channel.
product.3p: Cloud light, Cloud dark, Earth light, Earth dark. Registered in the real DSH theme service and available on this site. Packaged Windows rendering still requires GUI qualification.
product.4p: Charging and payment will be connected by the author. This site has no payment interface and does not collect payment data.
plugins.h: The hub stays empty; the spokes can change
plugins.p: Nine command skills are registered through the official ctx.skills, with 596 copied files matching pinned upstream hashes. This does not install third-party CLIs or grant execution/network/payment permissions; the release gate stays closed. Architecture and flow diagrams are planned with tt-a1i/archify (Apache-2.0, ships a DSH plugin).

faq.h: Clear up the easy misunderstandings first
faq.1q: Can I download Windows, Mac, or Linux installers now?
faq.1a: Not yet. This product has no accepted public installer. If 稟冊 has draft packages, those belong to a different app, and some download pages require a GitHub sign-in.
faq.2q: How can I use it now?
faq.2a: Get the source from GitHub and follow the Node, Git, and pnpm steps on the start page. Until a model provider is configured, do not claim that a model is available.
faq.3q: Is this the same product as Loop?
faq.3a: No. Loop is a completed independent project-management product. 湛箴_ymzz is the full DSH application plus plugins. Only the website visual language is referenced; there is no runtime import, migration or replacement.
faq.4q: Is my data sent to your servers?
faq.4a: This website does not collect accounts or conversations. Language and theme stay in your browser's localStorage. The product is local-first with zero telemetry. If you configure a cloud model yourself, that relationship is between you and that provider.
faq.5a: No. It is based on the MIT-licensed DeepSeek Harness and published by 晏銘湛箴. It does not represent DeepSeek officially.
faq.6a: Payment will be connected by the author and is not handled on this site. There is no pricing plan and no payment QR code here.

tagging.h: What you discussed, looked up and built stays findable
tagging.p: The panel lives in the native right-hand workspace and spans sessions. Sessions, visible reasoning text, visited pages, local files and artifacts are separate entries, assembled with many-to-many tags and Lists; the nebula groups by top-level tag, and one entry may sit in several clusters. Writing to the Vault requires human approval.
tagging.1p: Reads titles and messages through the native session query, taking only user messages, assistant replies and todos — never hidden chain-of-thought. Tags stay in the local ledger.
tagging.2p: The browser extension does not ship yet; the plan is to install it on the system drive with a guided setup. By design a record is written only when you press capture, and it never reads history or scans the disk.
tagging.3p: Local files and artifacts are registered by path; cloud works are registered by name and link only in v1, with no content sync — sync is left to a later version.
tagging.4p: Like Stars and Lists: tags can cross, merge and be revoked; the nebula caps at eight clusters, lays out deterministically and honours reduced motion.
tagging.note: This panel is in the source and unit-tested; Windows GUI and installers are not yet accepted. v1 ships without cloud sync; later versions may add it.
get.bundle: The planned desktop build uses Rust + Tauri 2 as a shell: one installer bundling the DSH runtime, Dashi Taskboard and T3 Code, with GitHub Actions tracking upstream releases to cut a daily canary. No accepted installer exists yet.
faq.7q: Does the tagging panel read my browsing history automatically?
faq.7a: No. There is no disk scan, no history read and no cloud sync. A page entry is written only when you press capture in the extension, and each entry can be deleted.
faq.8q: Where is the data, and can it go into Obsidian?
faq.8a: The ledger is a single local JSON under DSH_HOME/ymzz. Approved notes are written as Obsidian-compatible Markdown into the Vault you choose, with YAML frontmatter and wiki links; nothing is written before approval, and a write can be revoked.
faq.9a: Shell only: window, install, update and lifecycle. The full DeepSeek Harness still starts inside, and the left navigation, centre conversation, right workspace, four themes and native panels are not rewritten.

download.h: The first product tester starts on this page
download.status: Honest status: no stable (non-prerelease) installer is published or accepted yet; canary installers are CI-built prerelease assets labelled 未驗收. Download them as the first tester and report back via GitHub issues.
download.canary.hint: The developer channel in the home Get section lists prerelease assets labelled 未驗收 canary only after you opt in; they never become the main button. A version appears on the home page automatically once it passes real-machine acceptance.
download.step1.p: Open the prerelease entry on GitHub Releases and pick your platform. Asset names start with 湛箴_ymzz; assets from other products (including 稟冊) are unrelated.
download.step2.p: Compare the SHA256 from the release page first (canary builds are unsigned, so SmartScreen/Gatekeeper may warn about an unknown publisher — expected). Windows: run the NSIS installer; macOS: open the DMG and drag the app; Linux: chmod +x the AppImage and run it.
download.step3.p: The first launch asks for a nickname. Choose Add API Key → Set up later to skip the model key; without a provider the product claims no model capability. Configure model and MCP in native Settings afterwards.
download.step4.h: Test the tagging panel, then report
download.step4.p: Open the 知識 dock on the right: set a Vault via the native picker, turn a session or pasted text into a draft, approve it, commit into the Obsidian Vault, then try search, the nebula and revocation. Report anything broken on GitHub issues with version, platform, screenshot and steps.
download.feedback: Feedback: Ya-MiC/ymzz issues. The canary stage exists exactly to find what does not work.
download.boundary: This page hosts no pirated, cracked or third-party mirrors; installers come only from this repository's GitHub Releases.
download.privacy: Where data goes: see Privacy and cookies. The product has zero telemetry; model keys stay local.
